As relayed: a median of 55% (range 23–75%) reported any positive behaviour change across seven studies, while some used drugs as usual after a positive result because of withdrawal, tolerance, doubt about the result or wanting fentanyl. Only two of the 91 articles discuss overdose-related outcomes, neither with a control group (the review states this for the vending machine; the Vancouver comparisons are among checks); in the vending-machine evaluation, county overdose deaths fell by about 10% while Ohio's rose by about 5%, with naloxone dispensed by the same machine; the review concludes that only limited data suggest strip use decreases overdose rates or mortality.
